valueChange.when: The user selects another tab (pointer, an arrow key with automatic activation, Enter or Space).
valueChange.payload: The value of the selected tab.

rules: Arrange leading, label and trailing in that order, centered in the block dimension; label is required plain text in typography on one line, never truncated, and is the accessible name of the tab. leading holds at most one decorative icon of iconSize; trailing holds at most one Counter or Badge (a count of items in the panel, a New badge), sized by the tab.
The tab block size is minHeight; paddingInline on both sides, gap between parts.

With appearance line, an unselected tab paints its label and icon in idleColor in the default interaction and in content otherwise, and the selected tab paints them in selectedColor, the color of its indicator (user decision at the wave 4 Figma parity gate, 2026-11-12: the selected tab stands out from the others beyond its indicator); hover (the pointer over an unselected tab) paints surface behind it with radius corners. With appearance contained, every tab paints its label and icon in content, the selected tab being shown by its raised surface; hover paints surface behind an unselected tab with containedRadius corners. In both appearances the selected tab keeps its look under the pointer (activating it does nothing). interaction resolves in this order: disabled, hover, default.

With appearance contained, the selected tab is raised: painted in selectedSurfaceColor with shadowSelected, an edge of edgeThickness in elevationColor and containedRadius corners. With appearance line, the selected tab shows indicator, a bar of indicatorThickness in indicatorColor on the edge that faces the panels (the block end of a horizontal list, the inline end of a vertical list), over the list's line. Selection is never conveyed by color alone.
A disabled tab is shown in the disabled colors, cannot be selected, and is skipped by the arrow keys.
Colors and the indicator change over motionDuration with easingStandard; no transition under reduced motion.

Each panel holds the free content of the tab with the same value; only the panel of the selected tab is shown, the others are hidden from every user. The panel is exposed as a tab panel named by its tab. When its content has no focusable element, the panel itself is a stop in sequential focus after the list and shows the focus indicator of the tabs.

contrast.note: The label of the selected tab in a line list.
The label on its own surface in each interaction; disabled values are informational.
The selected tab of a contained list.
Unselected tabs on a contained list (the tint composited on color.surface.default).

rules: Tabs show one of several panels of related content at a time in the same place (sections of a settings page, views of a record), with a list of tabs to switch between them. They do not navigate to another page (that is a navigation menu with links), do not hold a form choice (that is a RadioGroup or a SegmentedControl) and never hide steps of a sequence.

list is exposed as a tab list named by label when it is non-empty; each trigger is a tab exposing whether it is selected and which panel it controls. There is always exactly one selected tab: value names it; when value matches no enabled tab, the first enabled tab is selected.

appearance contained (the default) shows the list as a container painted in listSurfaceColor with listRadius corners and listPadding around the tabs, the tabs separated by listGap so that a hovered tab and the selected tab never touch; in a horizontal list it fills the inline size it is given and the tabs share it equally, never narrower than their content; in a vertical list every tab is as wide as the widest. appearance line places the tabs on a line of lineThickness in lineColor along the edge that faces the panels, across the whole list, the tabs separated by listGap. orientation horizontal places the list above the panels, which start panelGap below it; orientation vertical places it at the inline start, the panels starting panelGap after it.

When a horizontal list does not fit its inline size, it scrolls inline without a visible scrollbar and keeps the focused tab and the selected tab visible; tabs never wrap or shrink. Each edge beyond which tabs are hidden shows a scroll button there, the tabs being invisible under it (fadeSize from the edge) and fading in over half of fadeSize after it; a tab scrolled into view clears that area. The scroll button is an IconButton of the tabs' size, intent neutral and appearance ghost, with a chevron towards that edge (mirrored in right-to-left text), that scrolls the list by most of its visible width. Scroll buttons are not stops in sequential focus and are hidden from assistive technology, since the arrow keys reach every tab; pointer, touch and trackpad scrolling also work.

Focus: the list is one stop in sequential focus, landing on the selected tab; Tab from the list moves to the selected panel (or its first focusable element). The roving focus rules are shared with Toolbar: in a horizontal list Right and Left Arrow (reversed in right-to-left text) move focus to the next and previous enabled tab, wrapping at the ends; in a vertical list Down and Up Arrow do; Home and End move it to the first and last enabled tab; disabled tabs are skipped.

With activation automatic, moving focus to a tab selects it; with activation manual, focus moves without selecting and Enter or Space selects the focused tab (for panels that are slow to show). A pointer press on an enabled tab selects it and focuses it. Selecting a tab emits valueChange when the value changed.
Each tab, and each panel that takes focus, shows a focus indicator of focusWidth in focusColor at focusOffset with focusRadius corners when focused by keyboard.
Setting value from the application selects the tab without emitting valueChange.
In forced-colors mode the list's line, the selected tab's indicator and the focus indicator stay visible in system colors, and disabled tabs use the system disabled text color.
